content:
We're hosting The Verification Summit on Wednesday, June 10 in San Francisco - a half-day, single-track event at the intersection of formal verification and AI. ~150 in the room, no parallel tracks, no ticket fee, approval-based.

The framing: most of the current conversation around "trustworthy AI" leans on probabilistic safety arguments and red-teaming. We think the more durable answers are the ones this community already works on: formal methods, theorem proving, runtime verification, proof-carrying code, alignment-by-construction - and we build heavily on Lean 4. The Summit exists to put the people doing that work in the same room as the founders and operators deploying AI into domains where hallucination isn't tolerable (regulated software, security, finance, scientific computing).

Agenda :

  • Sanjit Seshia (UC Berkeley EECS) - research talk on verified AI and cyber-physical systems
  • Fireside on the verification thesis with Vinod Khosla (Khosla Ventures)
  • Marco Pavone (Asst. prof at Stanford & Sr. Director at NVIDIA) - research talk on physical AI safety and autonomous systems
  • Panel on Verified AI across regulated domains (Speakers - distinguished industry veterans - list TBA)
  • Announcement of the Pramaana Labs Research Program: full scope shared during the event; but the call will be wide enough to include work coming out of the proof assistant / formalized math ecosystem.

Keynotes and the fireside will be published as recordings. So if you can't fly to SF, the technical content will still reach you.

This is for you if you're working on: Formal methods, theorem proving, runtime verification; deploying AI into domains that can't tolerate hallucination; or building the infrastructure underneath provable AI.

Site (agenda, application and other logistics): https://verificationsummit.ai
RSVP: https://luma.com/597otp0a
X : https://x.com/fv_summit (for updates on the agenda and logistics).

Happy to answer questions in this thread.

-- Krishnan
Pramaana Labs
